newsitem.title: GREECE: Dimitra Liani named sole heir in Papandreou's will.
newsitem.headline: Dimitra Liani named sole heir in Papandreou's will.

text.p: Dimitra Liani, the blonde widow of former Greek prime minister Andreas Papandreou, was named his sole heir and described as his "only great love" in two wills published in the Athens press on Friday.
"Dimitra is my life's great love," Papandreou said in one of his wills, handwriten in November 1990. "I leave all my property to her."
Papandreou sold most of his property to build her a pink villa in en exclusive northern Athens suburb. His remaining assets include a Mercedes limousine and various bank accounts.
The will, as well as a similar one dated May 1993, were both declared valid by an Athens court on Thursday.
Papandreou left nothing to his four children, saying in his will that his name was a good enough inheritance.
Liani, 41, a glamorous, ex-Olympic Airways flight attendant, stole his heart in 1988 while she was serving him drinks on an airliner.

Their flaunted extramarital affair shocked the nation. He divorced his second, American wife of 37 years to marry Liani in 1989 and for years she was branded an opportunist who exploited her relationship with Papandreou.
"When I go, Dimitra will certainly be in danger," Papandreou said in his will. "She will be held responsible for many things. So I call on all my friends to protect her by all means."
Papandreou, who ruled Greece from 1981 to 1985 and won a third term in October 1993, died in January. He was 77, 36 years older than Liani.

Liani stood by him through election defeat, financial scandals and open heart surgery and shared his stunning comeback in 1993. She was at his bedside while the veteran socialist fought for his life for more than four months with lung and kidney failure.

He appointed her head of his powerful private office, prompting strong criticism even within his party. That post and her ambition to run for parliament brought even more criticism than her nude bathing photos published in newspapers around the world.
Papandreou called on his children to denounce publicly his son-in-law Theodoros Katsanevas, a socialist party member, as a "disgrace to the family."

Papandreou accused Katsanevas of scheming to claim his political inheritance by "violently and illegally" occupying his office in the family home of Kastri, where the former premier kept his archives, personal items and library.
Katsanevas and his wife, Papandreou's daughter Sofia, said they were considering contesting that part of the will in court.
Liani and Papandreou's family are on notoriously bad terms although she was treated with apparent compassion and respect by his children during his funeral in June.
